source_text: τετήρηται καθαρῶς καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ τῷ τύπῳ τὸ σέβας, καὶ τὸ ἀκίβδηλον ἐν σκιαῖς, ἵνα μὴ τὸ τῆς ἀληθείας παρασημαίνηται κάλλος, ὡς ἐν ἐκείνοις ἠδικημένον. Ἀβέβηλος γὰρ ὁ Χριστὸς, καὶ οὐκ εἰδὼς ἁμαρτίαν, καὶ παντὸς ἐπέκεινα μολυσμοῦ, μᾶλλον δὲ λαμπρότητός τε καὶ καθαρότητος νοητῆς· εἴσω τε παντὸς ἁγιασμοῦ, κἂν εἰ ἐξίτηλον ἔχων τὸ ἔν γε τούτῳ διαφανὲς, διά τοι τὸ φυσικοῖς ἐρηρεῖσθαι νόμοις, καὶ ἀεὶ κατὰ τὰ αὐτὰ καὶ ὡσαύτως ἔχειν. Δηλοῖ δὲ, οἶμαι, τουτὶ, τὸ, «Ἀπὸ τῶν ἁγίων οὐκ ἐξελεύσεται, καὶ οὐ βεβηλώσει τὸ ἡγιασμένον τοῦ Θεοῦ αὐτοῦ.» Γυναῖκα δὲ δεῖν παρθένον πρὸς γάμου φέρεσθαι κοινωνίαν, εὖ μάλα φησὶ, καὶ ἀνάρμοστον ποιεῖται τὴν ἐξωσμένην. Ἣ καὶ εἰς τύπον ἂν εἴη τῆς Ἰουδαίων Συναγωγῆς· ἐκβέβληται γὰρ τῆς πρὸς αὐτὸν ἑνότητος, καὶ περὶ αὐτῆς φησι διὰ τῆς τοῦ προφήτου φωνῆς, ὅτι «Αὐτὴ οὐχ ἡ γυνή μου, καὶ ἐγὼ οὐκ ἀνὴρ αὐτῆς.» Ἡρμόσατο δὲ ὁ Παῦλος τὴν ἐξ ἐθνῶν Ἐκκλησίαν, παρθένον ἁγνὴν τῷ Χριστῷ, ἄσπιλον δὲ καὶ ἀρυτίδωτον, μᾶλλον δὲ ἁγίαν καὶ ἄμωμον. Οὕτω μὲν οὖν ἐπί τε τῆς ἐξ ἐθνῶν Ἐκκλησίας καὶ τῆς Ἰουδαίων μητρὸς, ἀληθὲς ἂν εἴη τὸ αἴνιγμα, καὶ ὁ τύπος οὐκ ἀκαλλής. Εἰ δὲ δὴ βούλοιτό τις πρὸς τὸν ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ λόγον περιτρέπειν ἀξίως τῶν ἐννοιῶν τὴν δύναμιν, φαμὲν, ὅτι ψυχαῖς βεβήλοις καὶ ἀνοσίαις, ἀσυναφὴς ὁ Χριστός· ταῖς δὲ πανάγνοις καὶ καθαραῖς, οἷάπερ παρθένοις, σύνεστι πνευματικῶς, καὶ ἐγκάρπους ἀποτελεῖ, καὶ γένος αὐτὰς οἰκεῖον ἀποκαλεῖ. «Ὅστις γὰρ ἂν ποιήσῃ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Πατρός μου,» φησὶ, «τοῦ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, οὗτος καὶ ἀδελφός μου, καὶ ἀδελφή μου, καὶ μήτηρ μού ἐστιν.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὀρθῶς ἔφης. {ΚΥΡ.} Ὁποίους μὲν οὖν εἶναι χρὴ τοὺς ἐξειλεγμένους εἰς ἱερουργίαν, ἄττα τε ὀρθῶς ἐπείγεσθαι δρᾷν, καὶ ὧν ἂν αὐτοὺς ἀπηλλάχθαι πρέποι, διακεχρησμῴδηκεν ἐναργῶς· ἀλλ' ἦν δή που πρὸς τῷδε σοφὸν, τὸ τίνα χρὴ τρόπον ἱερουργεῖν αὐτοὺς, ἐκφάνδην εἰπεῖν, καὶ καταῤῥυθμίσαι νόμοις, τά τε τῶν θυσιῶν εἴδη καὶ πᾶν τὸ ἱερουργούμενον, ὡς ἂν ἀμωμήτως ἔχοι τὸ πρᾶγμα αὐτοῖς, θυμηρεστάτην τε οὕτω ποιοῖντο τὴν λειτουργίαν. Οὐκοῦν καὶ πρό γε τῶν ἄλλων, «Οὐκ ἀναβήσῃ,» φησὶν, «ἐν ἀναβαθμοῖς ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριόν μου, ἵνα μὴ ἀποκαλύψῃς τὴν ἀσχημοσύνην σου ἐπ' αὐτό.» Ἀλλὰ πῶς ἂν τυχὸν γένοιτο τοῦτο, ἐρεῖ τις εὐθὺς, καίτοι ἐκ λίνου κατεσκευασμένον τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν ἐδίδου τὸ περισκελὲς, «ἵνα καλύπτῃ,» φησὶν, «ἀσχημοσύνην» χρωτὸς αὐτοῦ; Εἴπερ οὖν ἄρα, καὶ ὑψοῦ διᾴττειν ἐχρῆν, οὐδὲν ἂν ἠδίκησε τὸ χρῆμα αὐτοὺς περιεσταλμένους τὸ ἄσχημον. Ποῖ δὴ οὖν ἄρα τὸν τοῦ νόμου φαμὲν εἶναι σκοπόν; Τοῖς τῶν εἰδώλων προσκυνηταῖς, εὐκλεὲς εἶναί τε καὶ ἀναγκαῖον ἐδόκει, τὸ ὑψοῦ τοῖς τεμένεσιν ἱδρύσθαι βωμούς· καὶ οὐ πολὺς ἦν αὐτοῖς ὁ ἐπί γε τῷ χρῆναι σεμνῶς περιεστάλθαι λόγος.
pass_a_gloss: [in the case of Christ] the reverence has been kept purely even in the type itself, and the freedom from counterfeit in the shadows, so that the beauty of the truth might not be falsely marked, as if wronged in those things. For Christ is unprofaned, and not knowing sin, and beyond all defilement, or rather of radiance and spiritual purity; and within all holiness, even if having the clearness in this at least faded [in the type], because of being fixed in natural laws, and always being according to the same things and in the same way. And this, I think, is shown by: 'He shall not go out from the holy things, and he shall not profane the sanctified thing of his God.' And that a virgin wife must be brought to the fellowship of marriage he says very well, and makes unsuitable the one thrust out. And she would be for a type of the Synagogue of the Jews; for she has been cast out of the oneness with him, and about her he says through the voice of the prophet: 'She is not my wife, and I am not her husband.' But Paul betrothed the Church from the Gentiles, a pure virgin, to Christ, spotless and without wrinkle, or rather holy and blameless. So then, in the case of the Church from the Gentiles and of the mother of the Jews, the riddle would be true and the type not without beauty. And if anyone should wish to turn the force of the thoughts worthily to the meaning in each case, we say that to profane and unholy souls Christ is not joined; but with the all-pure and clean ones, as with virgins, he is present spiritually, and makes them fruitful, and calls them his own kin. 'For whoever does the will of my Father,' he says, 'who is in the heavens, this one is my brother, and sister, and mother.' PALL.: You spoke rightly. CYR.: What sort, then, those chosen for sacred service must be, and what things they rightly hasten to do, and from what it would befit them to be freed, he has clearly declared in oracles; but it was surely wise besides this to say openly in what way they must serve as priests, and to arrange by laws both the kinds of sacrifices and everything performed in sacred service, so that the matter might be blameless for them, and so they might make the ministry most pleasing. So then, before the others: 'You shall not go up,' he says, 'by steps upon my altar, so that you may not uncover your shame on it.' But how would this perhaps happen, someone will say at once, although he gave the priests the leg-covering made of linen, 'that it may cover,' he says, 'the shame' of his flesh? If then indeed they had to dart up high, the matter would have done them no wrong, being covered as to the unseemly. Where then do we say the aim of the law is? To the worshippers of idols it seemed glorious and necessary for altars to be set up high in the precincts; and not much was their account about the need to be decently covered.
pass_b_english: Cyril: …reverence has been kept pure even in the type itself, and the shadows have been kept free of anything counterfeit, so that the beauty of the truth should not be misrepresented, as though it had suffered harm in them. For Christ is free of all profanation; he knew no sin (2 Corinthians 5:21) and is beyond all defilement, or rather, he is all radiance and spiritual purity. He remains within all holiness, even if, here at least, its brightness has grown faint, because he stands firm on the laws of his own nature and is always the same and unchanging. This, I think, is what is meant by ‘He shall not go out of the holy place, and shall not profane what is consecrated to his God.’ (Leviticus 21:12) He says very rightly that he must take a virgin as his wife into the fellowship of marriage (Leviticus 21:13–14), and he declares the woman who has been driven out unfit for him. She may also stand as a type of the Synagogue of the Jews, for she has been cast out of union with him, and he says of her through the prophet’s voice: ‘She is not my wife, and I am not her husband.’ (Hosea 2:2) But Paul betrothed the Church from the Gentiles to Christ as a pure virgin (2 Corinthians 11:2), without spot or wrinkle, or rather holy and blameless (Ephesians 5:27). Taken in this way, of the Church from the Gentiles and of the mother of the Jews, the riddle would be true and the type not without beauty. But if someone wishes to apply the force of these ideas fittingly to each individual, we say that Christ has no union with profane and unholy souls; but with souls that are wholly chaste and pure, like virgins, he is joined spiritually, makes them fruitful, and calls them his own kin. For ‘whoever does the will of my Father in heaven,’ he says, ‘is my brother and my sister and my mother.’ (Matthew 12:50)
Palladius: You have put it rightly.

Cyril: He has plainly set out in his oracles what sort of men those chosen for sacred service must be, what they should rightly be eager to do, and what they ought to be free of. But it was surely wise, besides this, to state openly how they must perform the sacred rites, and to regulate by laws the kinds of sacrifices and everything that is offered, so that the whole matter might be blameless for them and they might in this way make their ministry most pleasing. So first of all he says: ‘You shall not go up by steps to my altar, so that you may not uncover your nakedness on it.’ (Exodus 20:26) But someone will say at once: how could this happen, when he gave the priests undergarments made of linen ‘to cover the nakedness’ of their flesh (Exodus 28:42)? Even if they had to climb up high, then, it would have done them no harm, since their nakedness was covered. What, then, shall we say the law is aiming at? The worshippers of idols thought it glorious and even necessary to set up altars high in their temple precincts, and they gave little thought to the need to be decently covered.

Opens mid-sentence, completing the clause begun at the end of section 18. Reviewer: the printed 'κἂν εἰ ἐξίτηλον ἔχων τὸ ἔν γε τούτῳ διαφανές' makes sense as it stands and is now translated, concessive included ('even if, here at least, its brightness has grown faint'): the holiness rests on Christ's own nature, so it stays whole even where the type shows it only faintly (compare 'the types are rather faint' in section 17). The earlier emendation to ἀνεξίτηλον and the dropped κἂν εἰ are withdrawn. Still worth a glance at the PG 68 column 817 scan. 'Or rather, he is all radiance and spiritual purity' takes the genitives λαμπρότητος … καθαρότητος νοητῆς as genitives of quality; another possible reading is 'beyond … even spiritual radiance and purity'. 'Knew no sin' cited to 2 Corinthians 5:21 (τὸν μὴ γνόντα ἁμαρτίαν). Hosea 2:2 is LXX/Hebrew Hosea 2:4. 'Mother of the Jews' means the Synagogue. Exodus 20:26 is Hebrew 20:23 in some printed Hebrew Bibles; Exodus 28:42 is 28:38 in some LXX editions. 'Temple precincts' renders τεμένεσιν.

Drafted Pass A, kept as written (rewritten as a literal English gloss from the Greek in pass_a_gloss): [continues 18: 'but for the great high priest, i.e. Christ,'] τετήρηται καθαρῶς (has been kept purely) even in the τύπος itself τὸ σέβας (reverence), and τὸ ἀκίβδηλον (the unadulterated) ἐν σκιαῖς, ἵνα μὴ τὸ τῆς ἀληθείας κάλλος παρασημαίνηται (be falsely stamped), as wronged in those. ἀβέβηλος ὁ Χριστός, οὐκ εἰδὼς ἁμαρτίαν, beyond every μολυσμός, μᾶλλον δὲ λαμπρότητός τε καὶ καθαρότητος νοητῆς (rather, of brightness and intelligible purity); εἴσω παντὸς ἁγιασμοῦ (within all sanctification), κἂν εἰ ἐξίτηλον ἔχων τὸ ἐν τούτῳ διαφανές [printed text: 'even if having the clearness in this fading' — see notes], διὰ τὸ φυσικοῖς ἐρηρεῖσθαι νόμοις (being fixed on natural laws) and ἀεὶ κατὰ τὰ αὐτὰ καὶ ὡσαύτως ἔχειν. this is shown by Lev 21:12 (not go out from the holy things, not profane τὸ ἡγιασμένον of his God). wife παρθένον for γάμου κοινωνίαν, εὖ μάλα φησί, and makes ἀνάρμοστον (unfitting) τὴν ἐξωσμένην (the thrust-out woman). she may be a type of the Jews' Synagogue: ἐκβέβληται τῆς πρὸς αὐτὸν ἑνότητος; through the prophet: 'she is not my wife and I am not her husband' (Hos 2:4 LXX). Paul ἡρμόσατο (betrothed) the Church ἐξ ἐθνῶν as παρθένον ἁγνὴν to Christ (2 Cor 11:2), ἄσπιλον καὶ ἀρυτίδωτον, rather ἁγίαν καὶ ἄμωμον (Eph 5:27). so applied to Church from nations and the Jews' mother, ἀληθὲς τὸ αἴνιγμα, ὁ τύπος οὐκ ἀκαλλής. if one wishes περιτρέπειν (turn) τῶν ἐννοιῶν τὴν δύναμιν πρὸς τὸν ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ λόγον (to the account about each one) worthily: to βεβήλοις καὶ ἀνοσίαις souls Christ ἀσυναφής (unjoined); with πανάγνοις καὶ καθαραῖς, as virgins, σύνεστι πνευματικῶς, ἐγκάρπους ἀποτελεῖ, calls them γένος οἰκεῖον. Mt 12:50. PALL.: ὀρθῶς ἔφης. CYR.: what sort ἐξειλεγμένους εἰς ἱερουργίαν must be, what rightly ἐπείγεσθαι δρᾶν, what ἀπηλλάχθαι πρέποι, διακεχρησμῴδηκεν ἐναργῶς (he has oracularly declared clearly). but wise besides: to say ἐκφάνδην τίνα τρόπον ἱερουργεῖν, καταρρυθμίσαι νόμοις the εἴδη of sacrifices and all ἱερουργούμενον, so that ἀμωμήτως ἔχοι, and they make λειτουργίαν θυμηρεστάτην. first: Ex 20:26 (not go up ἐν ἀναβαθμοῖς to my altar, lest ἀποκαλύψῃς ἀσχημοσύνην). objection: how could this happen, since he gave linen περισκελές 'to cover ἀσχημοσύνην χρωτός' (Ex 28:42)? even if ὑψοῦ διᾴττειν needed, no harm, being περιεσταλμένους τὸ ἄσχημον. ποῖ σκοπὸς τοῦ νόμου? to idol-worshippers εὐκλεὲς καὶ ἀναγκαῖον seemed to set βωμούς high in τεμένεσιν; οὐ πολὺς λόγος about σεμνῶς περιεστάλθαι.
